**Image analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Wheat/grass leaf held between fingers
- **Key features**:
  - Distinct linear, longitudinal stripes running parallel to leaf veins
  - Orange to rust-colored pustule lines with yellow-green halos/margins
  - Multiple parallel stripes following vascular bundles
  - Surrounding leaf tissue remains relatively green
  - Continuous linear pattern — not scattered discrete lesions

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Stripe Rust**: Classic presentation — yellow-orange uredinia arranged in linear rows running parallel to leaf veins, creating the characteristic "striped" pattern. The orange/rust pustule lines with yellow margins match very well.
- **Wheat Leaf Rust**: Shows scattered, circular/oval pustules, not organized in linear stripes — ruled out.
- **Tan Spot**: Discrete tan lesions with yellow halos, oval/lens-shaped — not linear stripes — ruled out.
- **Cephalosporium Stripe**: Pale yellow to white stripes, not orange/rust pustule rows — ruled out.
- **Bacterial Streak**: Water-soaked to tan/brown streaks between veins, not powdery orange pustules — ruled out.

The elongated, linear orange-yellow pustule rows running parallel to the veins are the hallmark of **Stripe Rust** (*Puccinia striiformis*).

This linear pustule arrangement along the vascular bundles is the defining characteristic of Puccinia striiformis, distinguishing it from leaf rust (scattered circular pustules) or tan spot (discrete oval lesions)."}
